en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 4.3.
Kusala-ttika, Cūḷantara-duka The Faultless Triplet and the Minor Intermediate Dyad.
4.3.1. The Triplet of the Wholesome and the Dyad of the Conditioned:
Dependent on a wholesome, conditioned state, a wholesome, conditioned state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome, conditioned state, an indeterminate, conditioned state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome, conditioned state, both wholesome, conditioned states and indeterminate,
conditioned states arise by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on an unwholesome, conditioned state, an unwholesome, conditioned state arises by way of root condition… [three].
Dependent on an indeterminate, conditioned state, an indeterminate, conditioned state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a wholesome, conditioned state and an indeterminate, conditioned state, an indeterminate, conditioned state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both an unwholesome, conditioned state and an indeterminate, conditioned state, an indeterminate, conditioned state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome conditioned state, a wholesome conditioned state arises by way of object condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome conditioned state, an unwholesome conditioned state arises by way of object condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate conditioned state, an indeterminate conditioned state arises by way of object condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-condition (hetu), there are nine; in the case of object-condition (ārammaṇa), three; in the case of predominance-condition (adhipati), nine … pe … in the case of result-condition (vipāka), one … pe … in the case of non-disappearance-condition (avigata), nine. (Abbreviated.
Negative (Paccanīya):
Not-root (Nahetu).
Dependent on an unwholesome state with a condition, an unwholesome state with a condition arises by way of the not-root condition (*na-hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on an indeterminate state with a condition, an indeterminate state with a condition arises by way of the not-root condition. (Abbreviated.

There are two [types] for the not-root condition, five for the not-object condition, nine for the not-predominance condition, seven for the not-prenascence condition, and [seven] for the not-postnascence condition.

In the case of non-repetition, nine; in the case of non-kamma, three; in the case of non-resultant, nine; in the case of non-nutriment …pe… in the case of non-path, one …pe… in the case of non-dissociation, three …pe… in the case of non-disappearance, five.
(Abbreviated. With root condition, in the case of non-object, five. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, two [answers] for object. (Abbreviated.
(The section on co-nascence ... pe ... and the section on association are similar to the section on dependence. Root-object.
A wholesome conditioned state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome conditioned state … three.
An unwholesome conditioned state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome conditioned state … three.
A neutral conditioned state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a neutral conditioned state.
A wholesome conditioned state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome conditioned state … three.
An unwholesome conditioned state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome conditioned state … three.
An indeterminate conditioned state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate conditioned state … three. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of cause-condition: seven; object-condition: nine; predominance-condition: ten; proximity-condition: seven ... [and so on] ... conascence-condition:
nine; mutuality-condition: three; dependence-condition: thirteen; strong-dependence-condition: nine; prenascence, postnascence, and repetition-conditions:
three; kamma-condition: seven; resultant-condition: one; nutriment ... [and so on] ... path-condition: seven; association-condition: three; dissociation-condition: five.
...pe... thirteen with non-disappearance.
(Abbreviated. Fifteen with not-root; fifteen with not-object. (Abbreviated.
Seven with root-condition and not-object. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, there are nine [answers] for the object condition. (Abbreviated.
Just as the section on questions in the wholesome triad (*kusalattika*), so it should be expanded in detail.
4.3.2. Wholesome Triad, Conditioned Dyad (*saṅkhataduka*).
Dependent on a wholesome conditioned state, a wholesome conditioned state arises by way of root condition.
(This is similar to the Sappaccaya-duka. 4.3.3. The Wholesome Triplet, the Visible Pair:
Dependent on a wholesome non-visible state, a wholesome non-visible state arises by way of root condition... three.
Dependent on an unwholesome, non-demonstrable phenomenon, an unwholesome, non-demonstrable phenomenon arises by way of root condition … three [cases].
Dependent on an indeterminate, non-demonstrable phenomenon, an indeterminate, non-demonstrable phenomenon arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a wholesome, non-demonstrable phenomenon and an indeterminate, non-demonstrable phenomenon, an indeterminate, non-demonstrable phenomenon arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on unwholesome and non-demonstrable states, and dependent on indeterminate and non-demonstrable states, an indeterminate and non-demonstrable state arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
Dependent on a wholesome and non-demonstrable state, a wholesome and non-demonstrable state arises by way of the object condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).
Dependent on an unwholesome and non-demonstrable state, an unwholesome and non-demonstrable state arises by way of the object condition.

Dependent on a neutral, non-demonstrable state, arises a neutral, non-demonstrable state by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are nine; under object-condition there are three ... pe ... under resultant-condition there is one ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition there are nine. (Abbreviated. Not-root-condition: [0] i. Dependent on a neutral, non-demonstrable state, arises a neutral, non-demonstrable state by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. ii. Dependent on a neutral, non-demonstrable state, arise states that are both root and non-demonstrable by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. iii. Dependent on a neutral, non-demonstrable state, arise states that are neither root nor demonstrable by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. iv. Dependent on a neutral, non-demonstrable state, arise states that are both root and demonstrable by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. v. Dependent on a neutral, non-demonstrable state, arise states that are both root and demonstrable, and states that are neither root nor demonstrable, by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. vi. Dependent on a neutral, non-demonstrable state, arise states that are neither root nor demonstrable, and states that are both root and non-demonstrable, by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. vii. Dependent on a neutral, non-demonstrable state, arise states that are both root and demonstrable, and states that are neither root nor demonstrable, and states that are both root and non-demonstrable, by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. viii. Dependent on a neutral, non-demonstrable state, arise states that are neither root nor demonstrable, and states that are both root and demonstrable, by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. ix.

Dependent on a neutral, non-demonstrable state, arise states that are neither root nor demonstrable, and states that are both root and non-demonstrable, and states that are both root and demonstrable, by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. [End of] Not-root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome, non-demonstrable state, an unwholesome, non-demonstrable state arises by way of the not-root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate, non-demonstrable state, an indeterminate, non-demonstrable state arises by way of the not-root condition.
(Abbreviated. Two for not-root; five for not-object; nine for not-predominance ... pe ... five for not-disappearance.
Root-object condition:
A wholesome non-visible phenomenon is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome non-visible phenomenon … three.
An unwholesome non-visible phenomenon is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome non-visible phenomenon … three.
An indeterminate, non-demonstrable state is a condition for an indeterminate, non-demonstrable state by way of the root-condition.
A wholesome, non-demonstrable state is a condition for a wholesome, non-demonstrable state by way of the object-condition … three [ways].
An unwholesome, non-demonstrable state is a condition for an unwholesome, non-demonstrable state by way of the object-condition … three [ways].
An indeterminate and non-demonstrable state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate and non-demonstrable state... three. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are seven;

under object-condition, nine; under predominance-condition, ten; under proximity-condition, seven... pe ... under decisive-support-condition, nine... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition, thirteen. (Abbreviated.
(As the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet, so it should be expanded.)

4.3.4. The Wholesome Triplet, the With-Resistance Dyad Dependent on a root, indeterminate, with-resistance state, an indeterminate, with-resistance state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition: one [answer] … pe … in the case of non-disappearance: one. (Abbreviated.
(Also in the section on co-nascence … pe … and in the section on inquiry, there is one in every instance.
Dependent on a wholesome, non-reactive state, a wholesome, non-reactive state arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on an unwholesome non-reactive state, an unwholesome non-reactive state arises by way of root condition … three [cases].
Dependent on an indeterminate non-reactive state, an indeterminate non-reactive state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a wholesome non-reactive state and an indeterminate non-reactive state, an indeterminate non-reactive state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on unwholesome non-reactive phenomena and indeterminate non-reactive phenomena, an indeterminate non-reactive phenomenon arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on wholesome non-reactive phenomena, a wholesome non-reactive phenomenon arises by way of object-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome non-reactive state, an unwholesome non-reactive state arises by way of object-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate non-reactive state, an indeterminate non-reactive state arises by way of object-condition.

(Abbreviated. In the case of root-cause: nine; in the case of object: three; in the case of predominance: nine ... pe ... in the case of result: one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance: nine. (Abbreviated.)
Dependent on a non-root unwholesome non-reactive state, a non-root unwholesome non-reactive state arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate non-reactive state, an indeterminate non-reactive state arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root: two; with not-object: five; with not-predominance: nine ... pe ... with not-disappearance: five. (Abbreviated.
(The "Conascent" section ... pe ... and the "Associated" section are the same as the "Dependent" section.
Root.
A wholesome non-reactive state is a condition for a wholesome non-reactive state by way of the root-condition … three.
An unwholesome non-reactive state is a condition for an unwholesome non-reactive state by way of the root-condition … three.
A neutral non-reactive state is a condition for a neutral non-reactive state by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-cause (hetu), there are seven; in the case of object (ārammaṇa), nine; in the case of predominance (adhipati), ten ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance (avigata), thirteen. 4.3.5.
The Wholesome Triplet (Kusalattika) and the Material Dyad (Rūpīduka):
Root-cause.
Dependent on an indeterminate material phenomenon, an indeterminate material phenomenon arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there is one; under object condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance condition there is one. (Abbreviated.
(In the section on co-nascence as well … pe … in the section on inquiry as well, there is one in every instance.)
Dependent on a wholesome immaterial state, a wholesome immaterial state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome immaterial state, an unwholesome immaterial state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate immaterial state, an indeterminate immaterial state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to root-cause: three; with respect to object: three ... pe ... with respect to result: one; with respect to non-disappearance:
three. (Abbreviated. With respect to not-root: two; with respect to not-predominance: three ... pe ... with respect to not-resultant: three; with respect to not-jhāna and not-kamma:
one; with respect to not-dissociation: three. (Abbreviated. (The Chapter on Conascent, ... pe ... and the Chapter on Associated, are also the same as the Chapter on Dependent.)
Root-object condition:
A wholesome immaterial state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome immaterial state.
An unwholesome immaterial state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome immaterial state.
An indeterminate immaterial state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate immaterial state.
A wholesome immaterial state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome immaterial state—three [cases].
An unwholesome immaterial state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome immaterial state—three [cases].
An indeterminate immaterial state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate immaterial state.
(Abbreviated. Under root: three; under object: nine; under predominance: seven; under proximity: seven ... pe ... under conascence, mutuality, and dependence:
three; under decisive support: nine; under repetition: three; under kamma: five; under result: one; under nutriment ... pe ...
With associated [condition], three; ... pe ... with non-disappearance, three. (Abbreviated.

4.3.6. *Kusala-ttika*, *Lokiya-duka*.
Dependent on a wholesome mundane state, a wholesome mundane state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome mundane state, an indeterminate mundane state arises by way of root condition. A wholesome mundane...
Dependent on a wholesome mundane state, both unwholesome mundane states and indeterminate mundane states arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome mundane state, an unwholesome mundane state arises by way of root condition … three [combinations].
Dependent on an indeterminate mundane state, an indeterminate mundane state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on wholesome mundane phenomena and indeterminate mundane phenomena, an indeterminate mundane phenomenon arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on unwholesome mundane phenomena and indeterminate mundane phenomena, an indeterminate mundane phenomenon arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are nine;
under object condition there are three ... pe ... under result condition there is one ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are nine. (Abbreviated.)
Dependent on a non-causal unwholesome mundane state, a non-causal unwholesome mundane state arises by way of the non-root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate mundane state, an indeterminate mundane state arises by way of the non-root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the absence of root-condition (na-hetu), there are two; in the absence of object-condition (na-ārammaṇa), five; in the absence of predominance-condition (na-adhipati), nine …pe… in the absence of disappearance-condition (na-vigata), five. Root-object:
A wholesome mundane state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome mundane state … three.
An unwholesome mundane state is a condition for an unwholesome mundane state by way of the root-condition … three.
A neutral mundane state is a condition for a neutral mundane state by way of the root-condition.
A wholesome mundane state is a condition for a wholesome mundane state by way of the object-condition … three.
An unwholesome mundane state is a condition for an unwholesome mundane state by way of object-condition … three.
An indeterminate mundane state is a condition for an indeterminate mundane state by way of object-condition … three.
(Abbreviated. Under root: seven; under object: nine; under predominance: nine … pe … under non-disappearance: thirteen.
4.3.6.2. Supramundane State:
Root Condition.
Dependent on a wholesome supramundane state, a wholesome supramundane state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate supramundane state, an indeterminate supramundane state arises by way of root condition.

(Abbreviated. Two under root; two under object; two under predominance ... pe ... one under repetition and fruition ... pe ... two under non-disappearance. (Abbreviated. Two under non-predominance ... pe ... one under non-repetition, non-kamma, and non-fruition; two under non-dissociation. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on “Conascent” and “Associated” are likewise similar to the section on “Dependent. Root, Object, etc.:
A wholesome supramundane state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome supramundane state.
An indeterminate supramundane state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate supramundane state.

An indeterminate supramundane state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate supramundane state. An indeterminate supramundane state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome supramundane state.
A wholesome supramundane state is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a wholesome supramundane state.

An indeterminate supramundane state is a condition for an indeterminate supramundane state by way of predominance-condition (*adhipati-paccaya*). An indeterminate supramundane state is a condition for a wholesome supramundane state by way of predominance-condition.
A wholesome supramundane state is a condition for an indeterminate supramundane state by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
An indeterminate supramundane state is a condition for an indeterminate supramundane state by way of proximity-condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root-condition, two; object-condition, two; predominance-condition, three; proximity-condition, two; contiguity-condition, two;

conascence-condition, two; mutuality-condition, two; dependence-condition, two; decisive support-condition, four ... [and so on] ... kamma-condition, three; resultant-condition, one ... [and so on] ...
non-disappearance-condition, two. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so it should be expanded in detail.
4.3.7. *Kusalattika*, *Kenaciviññeyyaduka*, and *Paccayacatukka*.
Conditioned by a wholesome state cognizable by anyone, a wholesome state cognizable by anyone arises by way of root condition.
Conditioned by a wholesome state cognizable by anyone, an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone arises by way of root condition.
Conditioned by a wholesome state cognizable by anyone, a wholesome state cognizable by anyone...
And indeterminate states cognizable by anyone arise with a root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state cognizable by anyone, an unwholesome state cognizable by anyone arises with a root condition… three [combinations].
Dependent on an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone, an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone arises with a root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state cognizable by anyone and an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone, an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
Dependent on an unwholesome state cognizable by anyone and an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone, an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state cognizable by anyone, a wholesome state cognizable by anyone arises by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).
Dependent on an unwholesome state cognizable by anyone, an unwholesome state cognizable by anyone arises by way of object-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone, an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone arises by way of object-condition.
(Abbreviated. In the case of root-cause, nine; in the case of object, three ... pe ... in the case of result, one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, nine. (Abbreviated.)
By way of non-root condition: in dependence on an unwholesome state cognizable by anyone, an unwholesome state cognizable by anyone arises by way of non-root condition.
In dependence on an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone, an indeterminate state cognizable by anyone arises by way of non-root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, two; with not-object condition, five; with not-predominance condition, nine …pe… with not-disappearance condition, five.
Root:
A wholesome state cognizable by anyone is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state cognizable by anyone … three.
An unwholesome state cognizable by anyone is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state cognizable by anyone. … three.
A neutral state cognizable by anyone is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a neutral state cognizable by anyone.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is not cognizable by any [particular] means, a wholesome state that is not cognizable by any [particular] means arises by way of root-condition. (This is similar to [the section on] "cognizable by some.
